name: issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_within_deadband_no_escalate
description: REVISED under Issue #843, superseding this scenario's original #827 premise -- kept under its original name/issue tag so the revision is traceable, not silently swapped. The #827 premise was: a small, sub-deadband dawn dip on a hot day should NEVER escalate to heat, no matter how long it persists, because the day is forecast to self-correct as the sun comes up (a purely forecast-based, recency-blind tolerance). Issue #843 explicitly redefines the against-grain deadband's role: it is only a short-cycling guard against RECENT opposite-family activity, not a general 'day will self-correct, tolerate indefinitely' mechanism -- confirmed with the project owner directly (2026-09-04) after this exact scenario failed the Issue #843 regression check and the conflict was surfaced for a decision, not resolved silently. With nothing cooling-side ever recorded (a cold start, same as this scenario's original setup), the against-grain deadband is now 0 -- the breach escalates once sustain-confirmed, the same as every other 'nothing recent' case in test_comfort_family_decision.py's TestRecencyGatedDeadband. See issue_827_hot_day_deadband_cleared_escalates.json for a scenario that was ALREADY escalate-on-breach even under the old design (a large 7F breach past the literal deadband) -- this scenario's revision brings the small-breach/cold-start case into alignment with that one, rather than leaving a day-type-specific exception.
source: Issue #843 (recency-gated deadband) -- revises Issue #827 Design #1's mid-review correction after the project owner confirmed the recency rule should apply uniformly across all day types, including hot/cold-day dawn dips previously exempted for energy-savings reasons.
notes: (a) Scenario effectiveness (revert-test): if Issue #843's recency gate were reverted (deadband applied unconditionally regardless of recency, the pre-#843/#827-only design), this 3F breach (68-65=3, within the 5F hot-day deadband) would stay WITHIN_DEADBAND forever and the final assertions (comfort_family='heating', last_hvac_mode='heat') would FAIL -- proving this scenario genuinely depends on the recency gate treating a never-recorded cooling history as 'not recent', not on the breach magnitude alone.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md #6f's deadband table and const.py's CONF_COMFORT_DEADBAND_* block comment both now document the against-grain deadband as CONDITIONAL on comfort_family_recency_window_min -- this scenario is the hot-day test reference for the 'nothing ever recorded' cold-start case, replacing its own prior no-escalate reference.

(c) Occupant experience: with nothing cooling-side having run in this scenario at all, there is nothing for the deadband to protect against -- a 3F sub-floor dip at dawn now corrects itself via the furnace within a couple of minutes rather than the occupant coasting below comfort for up to two hours on the hope the day warms up in time. The energy cost is a few minutes of furnace runtime; the alternative the old design accepted was multiple hours of a house colder than its own comfort floor promises, the same category of occupant-facing problem the reported overnight-drift bug (Issue #843's original trigger) was about.

events.note: Hot-day classification at dawn. base_family='cooling' (native). Cold start -- nothing cooling-side has ever run, so minutes_since_cooling_ended is None (not recent).

Dawn dip: indoor drops to 65F, 3F below comfort_heat(68). Pre-#843 this was within comfort_deadband_hot_f (5.0F) and held indefinitely; under #843, with nothing cooling-side recorded, the effective deadband is 0 -- this breach immediately arms a heat candidate.
Re-evaluation: heat_breach_delta = 68-65 = 3F > 0 (recency-gated deadband) -- candidate arms, not yet sustain-confirmed (elapsed 0s < 90s). Stays 'cooling' this tick.
120s later (>90s sustain window). First-ever transition for this engine (cold start, no dwell gate). Sustain-confirmed: comfort family escalates to heating, commands heat at comfort_heat(68).

assertions.reason: Baseline: hot day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.
Issue #843: with nothing cooling-side ever recorded, the against-grain deadband is 0 regardless of the 3F breach being 'small' -- once sustain-confirmed, the family escalates to heating.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: REVISED under Issue #843: a dawn dip below comfort_heat on a hot-classified day now escalates to heat once sustain-confirmed, even though the breach itself is small, because nothing cooling-side has run recently -- there is nothing for the against-grain deadband to protect against. Supersedes this scenario's original #827 verdict (indefinite tolerance based on forecast self-correction alone), per explicit project-owner confirmation that the recency rule applies uniformly across day types.
verdict.observed_behavior: Indoor drops to 65F (3F below the 68F floor) at dawn with no prior cooling-side activity recorded -- comfort family escalates to heating at 06:17:00 once sustain-confirmed, and heat is commanded at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: The against-grain deadband is a short-cycling guard conditioned on recent opposite-family activity (Issue #843), not a day-type-scaled forecast-based tolerance (the retired #827 framing) -- a cold start with nothing recorded behaves like the native direction (near-zero deadband, still sustain-confirmed) for every day type, hot/cold included.
